season.evidence: Web pages put the best window at mid-August to early October (bugs fade, road gate open from July 1, early-October fall color); stored Aug-Oct.

track.why: 2026-09-06 round trip starting 18 m and ending 7 m from our Cougar Divide trailhead pin, summit 3 m from our pin; the line follows Cougar Divide then Chowder Ridge, the only way up from this trailhead (the Skyline Divide route starts elsewhere). No logged route name, but a single route starts at this trailhead.

otherTracksConsidered.why: 2026-08-15 round trip, in season, also complete; second choice.
2026-10-18 complete but the track continues south past the summit, highest point 2397 m, so it is not a clean line to Hadley.

facts.text: In August one rough, eroded stretch of the forest road about ten minutes below the trailhead needs care; one party in mid-August parked 2.7 miles short and walked, but a spot roughly half a mile closer was available.
Mosquitoes and biting flies swarm at the trailhead in August; start walking at once.
In August about 20 trees lay across the trail; the way past the Cougar Divide high point is faint and hard to follow where it climbs rock and sand toward Chowder Ridge.
Small streams on the ridge give better water than the stagnant ponds passed on the way up in August.
Loose choss and scree on the final scramble make a helmet worthwhile, and a big group risks rockfall because there is little room to spread out.
In mid-October the exposed rock tooth near the summit block can be bypassed on its lower side, which keeps the scramble at about class 2 but over loose rock.
Wild blueberries are ripening by mid-August along the first stretch of trail.

season.evidence: Web pages: Skyline Divide a popular mid-summer to fall hike; route already has a track so no scope here.

notes: Skyline Divide already has 743 track points; it is listed in allRoutesOnPeak only. Peakbagger summit 7521.7 ft.
